```tsx
import { useId, useState } from 'react'
import { BottomSheetHeader } from '@l3/components/BottomSheet'
import { Button } from '@l3/components/Button'
import { ButtonGroup } from '@l3/components/ButtonGroup'
import { Checkbox } from '@l3/components/Checkbox'
import { Icon } from '@l3/components/Icon'
import { ListCell } from '@l3/components/ListCell'
import { msDelete } from '@l3/icons/material'
import { Sheet } from '../../../shared/ui/Sheet'
import { t } from '../copy'
import styles from './ChatSheets.module.css'

/**
 * Delete this chat? — large header with the bin (like Delete rule). A checkbox, off by default, also deletes everything
 * the chat created — one chat can make several things of any kind (rules, indicators, strategies: the field's pills
 * only hint DASH, they don't limit it). Left off, only the conversation goes; its creations stay in Your creations.
 */
export function DeleteChatSheet({ onClose, onDelete }: {
  onClose: () => void
  /** `withCreation`: the checkbox was ticked. */
  onDelete: (withCreation: boolean) => void
}) {
  const headingId = useId()
  const [withCreation, setWithCreation] = useState(false)
  return (
    <Sheet
      labelledBy={headingId}
      onClose={onClose}
      header={<BottomSheetHeader size="lg" headingId={headingId} heading={t('chatMenu.deleteTitle')} description={t('chatMenu.deleteText')} icon={<span className={styles.binIcon}><Icon icon={msDelete} size={24} /></span>} />}
      footer={
        <ButtonGroup aria-label={t('chatMenu.deleteTitle')} direction="vertical">
          <Button onClick={() => onDelete(withCreation)}>{t('chatMenu.deleteConfirm')}</Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onClose}>{t('chatMenu.deleteKeep')}</Button>
        </ButtonGroup>
      }
    >
      <ListCell
        as="label"
        variant="card"
        multiline
        label={t('chatMenu.alsoDelete')}
        description={t('chatMenu.alsoDeleteText')}
        trailing={<Checkbox checked={withCreation} onChange={(e) => setWithCreation(e.target.checked)} />}
      />
    </Sheet>
  )
}
```

### `src/flows/dash/sheets/IndicatorSheets.tsx`

```tsx
import { useId, useState } from 'react'
import { Button } from '@l3/components/Button'
import { ButtonGroup } from '@l3/components/ButtonGroup'
import { Stack } from '@l3/components/Stack'
import { Sheet } from '../../../shared/ui/Sheet'
import { RuleSummary } from '../components/RuleSummary'
import { SuccessBurst } from '../components/SuccessBurst'
import { PineActions } from '../components/PineActions'
import { t } from '../copy'
import type { IndicatorDraft } from '../indicatorData'
// Same layout as "Your rule is created" (tick burst, title, line, summary, two buttons).
import styles from './RuleSheets.module.css'

const TICK_FLIP_MS = 150

/**
 * After Save indicator (Version 2): the indicator is created and saved — the tick bursts, a summary of what was saved,
 * Done (back to the chat) and View indicator (Scalper's Indicators sheet, with it under Your indicators).
 */
export function IndicatorSavedSheet({ draft, onDone, onView }: { draft: IndicatorDraft; onDone?: () => void; onView?: () => void }) {
  const id = useId()
  // View indicator: the tick turns away first, then Scalper opens (as View Rules does).
  const [leaving, setLeaving] = useState(false)
  const view = () => {
    setLeaving(true)
    window.setTimeout(() => onView?.(), TICK_FLIP_MS)
  }
  return (
    <Sheet
      labelledBy={id}
      onClose={onDone}
      footer={
        // Vertical dock, like Your rule is created: View indicator (primary) on top, Close (secondary) under it.
        <ButtonGroup aria-label={t('indicatorSaved.title')} direction="vertical">
          <Button onClick={view}>{t('indicatorSaved.view')}</Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onDone}>{t('created.close')}</Button>
        </ButtonGroup>
      }
    >
      <Stack gap="24" align="stretch" className={styles.content}>
        <Stack gap="16" align="center" className={styles.centre}>
          <SuccessBurst leaving={leaving} />
          <Stack gap="08" align="center">
            <h2 id={id} className={styles.title}>{t('indicatorSaved.title')}</h2>
            <p className={styles.description}>{t('indicatorSaved.description')}</p>
          </Stack>
        </Stack>
        {/* The indicator, then its Pine Script (Copy / Share / Download — kept out of the chat; here and in the history
            details sheet), 16 apart. */}
        <Stack gap="16">
          <RuleSummary title={draft.name} description={t('indicatorSaved.summary', { place: draft.placement, count: draft.testedOn })} />
          <PineActions name={draft.name} />
        </Stack>
      </Stack>
    </Sheet>
  )
}
```

```tsx
import { useId } from 'react'
import { BottomSheetHeader } from '@l3/components/BottomSheet'
import { Button } from '@l3/components/Button'
import { ButtonGroup } from '@l3/components/ButtonGroup'
import { Card } from '@l3/components/Card'
import { Icon } from '@l3/components/Icon'
import { msAutorenew, msMonitoring, msUploadFile } from '@l3/icons/material'
import { Sheet } from '../../../shared/ui/Sheet'
import pineScript from '../assets/pine-script.svg'
import { t } from '../copy'
import styles from './PineUploadSheet.module.css'

/**
 * What the + in the chat field is for (so it's clear even without the first-time tip): uploading a Pine Script.
 * Laid out like the Kill Switch info sheet (~/kill-switch-l3 "Protect your trades"): a soft DASH-green wash behind the
 * large header (Pine Script mark, title, line), then how it works as three single lines in one card, each with a grey
 * icon box — pick the script, DASH converts it, it's on your Scalper chart — and a note that pasting it works too. Choose a file opens the picker; Not
 * now closes it.
 */
export function PineUploadSheet({ onChoose, onClose }: { onChoose: () => void; onClose: () => void }) {
  const id = useId()
  const steps = [
    { icon: msUploadFile, text: t('pineSheet.step1') },
    { icon: msAutorenew, text: t('pineSheet.step2') },
    { icon: msMonitoring, text: t('pineSheet.step3') },
  ]
  return (
    <Sheet
      labelledBy={id}
      onClose={onClose}
      header={<BottomSheetHeader size="lg" className={styles.header} headingId={id} heading={t('pineSheet.title')} description={t('pineSheet.description')} icon={<span className={styles.logo}><Icon icon={pineScript} size={24} /></span>} />}
      footer={
        // The paste note sits in the dock, right above Choose a file.
        <ButtonGroup aria-label={t('pineSheet.title')} direction="vertical">
          <p className={styles.note}>{t('pineSheet.paste')}</p>
          <Button onClick={onChoose}>{t('pineSheet.choose')}</Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onClose}>{t('pineSheet.notNow')}</Button>
        </ButtonGroup>
      }
    >
      <Card as="section" aria-label={t('pineSheet.how')}>
        <ul className={styles.steps}>
          {steps.map((step) => (
            <li key={step.text} className={styles.step}>
              <span className={styles.stepIcon}><Icon icon={step.icon} size={16} /></span>
              {step.text}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </Card>
    </Sheet>
  )
}
```

```css
/* DASH sheets: L3 bottom sheets; the read-more and saved sheets carry DASH's tint at the top. */
/* The L3 sheet content already brings 16 / 16 / 24; these pages add 8 on top (Figma: 24 above the art). */
.content {
  padding-top: var(--l3-spacing-08);
}

.centre {
  text-align: center;
}

.roomy {
  padding-block: var(--l3-spacing-48) var(--l3-spacing-08);
}

.title {
  margin: 0;
  font: var(--l3-text-heading-20);
  color: var(--l3-content-primary);
}

.description {
  margin: 0;
  font: var(--l3-text-label-14);
  color: var(--l3-content-tertiary);
  text-wrap: balance;
}

/* Read more: a top-down tint in the result's light accent (Figma: green for saved, pink for cost, none for no data). */
.tinted {
  --tint: transparent;
  /* edge to edge: out of the sheet's 16 content padding, then the same 16 back inside */
  margin: calc(-1 * var(--l3-spacing-16)) calc(-1 * var(--l3-spacing-16)) 0;
  padding: var(--l3-spacing-16) var(--l3-spacing-16) 0;
  background: linear-gradient(to bottom, var(--tint), var(--l3-surface-default) 45%);
}

.tinted[data-result='saved'] { --tint: var(--l3-surface-accent-success-light); }
.tinted[data-result='cost'] { --tint: var(--l3-surface-accent-error-light); }

/* The orb on a soft white disc with a thin DASH edge (Figma: 88, 1px lime at 40%). */
.orbDisc {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: var(--l3-size-80);
  height: var(--l3-size-80);
  border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--app-dash-green) 40%, transparent);
  border-radius: var(--l3-radius-full);
  background: radial-gradient(circle, var(--l3-surface-default) 55%, color-mix(in srgb, var(--app-dash-glow-1) 15%, var(--l3-surface-default)));
}

/* Version 2 delete: the icon in a 64 red circle (the large header's icon slot). */
.deleteIcon {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: var(--l3-size-64);
  height: var(--l3-size-64);
  border-radius: var(--l3-radius-full);
  background: var(--l3-surface-accent-error-light);
  color: var(--l3-content-accent-error-default);
}

/* Version 2 details: centred, like "Your rule is created". */
.details {
  padding-top: var(--l3-spacing-08);
  text-align: center;
}

/* Card style New · a Smart Rule's details: what Smart Rule means (the card has just the tag). */
.smartNote {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  gap: var(--l3-spacing-08);
  margin: 0;
  padding: var(--l3-spacing-12);
  border-radius: var(--l3-radius-12);
  background: var(--l3-surface-secondary);
  color: var(--l3-content-secondary);
  font: var(--l3-text-description-12);
  text-align: center;
}

/* Card style New · details */
.activityValue {
  font: var(--l3-text-label-12);
  color: var(--l3-content-secondary);
  text-align: end;
}

.activityValue strong {
  font: var(--l3-text-heading-12);
  color: var(--l3-content-primary);
}

/* Details version 2: the Status tag is the switch (a plain button around the L3 Tag; tap target grows past the tag). */
.statusSwitch {
  position: relative;
  display: inline-flex;
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  background: none;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.statusSwitch::after {
  content: '';
  position: absolute;
  inset: calc(-1 * var(--l3-spacing-12));
}

/* Details version 3: one toggle card — Status in Heading/14, the activity under it, the status word + switch right. */
.statusHeading {

.statusToggle {
```

```tsx
import { useId, useState } from 'react'
import { BottomSheetHeader } from '@l3/components/BottomSheet'
import { Button } from '@l3/components/Button'
import { ButtonGroup } from '@l3/components/ButtonGroup'
import { Icon } from '@l3/components/Icon'
import { ListCell } from '@l3/components/ListCell'
import { Stack } from '@l3/components/Stack'
import { Switch } from '@l3/components/Switch'
import { Tag } from '@l3/components/Tag'
import { msDelete, msEdit } from '@l3/icons/material'
import { Sheet } from '../../../shared/ui/Sheet'
import { DashOrb } from '../../../shared/ui/dash/DashOrb'
import { BacktestStrip } from '../components/RuleCard'
import { PineActions } from '../components/PineActions'
import { SuccessBurst } from '../components/SuccessBurst'
import { RuleSummary } from '../components/RuleSummary'
import { t } from '../copy'
import type { Backtest, DraftRule } from '../data'
import styles from './RuleSheets.module.css'

/**
 * Read more — the rule in full (Figma "Clicking on read more" ×3): the orb on a soft disc over a tint of the result,
 * the rule's name and sentence, and what the backtest found (nothing when there's no data).
 */
export function ReadMoreSheet({ rule, backtest, onClose }: { rule: DraftRule; backtest: Backtest; onClose?: () => void }) {
  const id = useId()
  return (
    <Sheet
      labelledBy={id}
      onClose={onClose}
      footer={
        <ButtonGroup aria-label={rule.title}>
          <Button onClick={onClose}>{t('readMore.okay')}</Button>
        </ButtonGroup>
      }
    >
      <div className={styles.tinted} data-result={backtest.result}>
        <Stack gap="24" align="stretch" className={styles.content}>
          <Stack gap="16" align="center" className={styles.centre}>
            <span className={styles.orbDisc}>
              <DashOrb size="md" />
            </span>
            <Stack gap="08" align="center">
              <h2 id={id} className={styles.title}>{rule.title}</h2>
              <p className={styles.description}>{rule.description}</p>
            </Stack>
          </Stack>
          {backtest.result !== 'none' && <BacktestStrip backtest={backtest} shape="pill" />}
        </Stack>
      </div>
    </Sheet>
  )
}

/** How long the tick's coin-turn runs before View Rules moves on (= motion/duration-short). */
const TICK_FLIP_MS = 150

/** Saved (Figma "Rule saved" 5612:41875): the tick pops in with confetti (live app motion), what happens now, the rule, Cancel / View Rules. */
export function RuleCreatedSheet({ rule, onCancel, onViewRules }: { rule: DraftRule; onCancel?: () => void; onViewRules?: () => void }) {
  const id = useId()
  // View Rules: the tick turns away first (150 ms), then the rules list fades in (live app).
  const [leaving, setLeaving] = useState(false)
  const viewRules = () => {
    setLeaving(true)
    window.setTimeout(() => onViewRules?.(), TICK_FLIP_MS)
  }
  return (
    <Sheet
      labelledBy={id}
      onClose={onCancel}
      footer={
        // Vertical dock: View rule (primary) on top, Close (secondary) under it.
        <ButtonGroup aria-label={t('created.title')} direction="vertical">
          <Button onClick={viewRules}>{t('created.viewRule')}</Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onCancel}>{t('created.close')}</Button>
        </ButtonGroup>
      }
    >
      <Stack gap="24" align="stretch" className={styles.content}>
        <Stack gap="16" align="center" className={styles.centre}>
          <SuccessBurst leaving={leaving} />
          <Stack gap="08" align="center">
            <h2 id={id} className={styles.title}>{t('created.title')}</h2>
            <p className={styles.description}>{t('created.description')}</p>
          </Stack>
        </Stack>
        <RuleSummary title={rule.title} description={rule.description} />
      </Stack>
    </Sheet>
  )
}

/** Delete? (Figma "Delete rule" 5612:42250): the question as the header, the rule, No / Yes, Delete. */
export function DeleteRuleSheet({ rule, heading = t('delete.title'), large = false, onNo, onYes }: { rule: { title: string; summary: string }; /** What's being deleted (default: a rule). */ heading?: string; /** Version 2: the large header with the delete icon in a red circle; Yes, Delete above No. */ large?: boolean; onNo?: () => void; onYes?: () => void }) {
  const id = useId()
  if (large) {
    return (
      <Sheet
        labelledBy={id}
        onClose={onNo}
        header={<BottomSheetHeader size="lg" headingId={id} heading={heading} icon={<span className={styles.deleteIcon}><Icon icon={msDelete} size={24} /></span>} />}
        footer={
          <ButtonGroup aria-label={heading} direction="vertical">
            <Button onClick={onYes}>{t('delete.yes')}</Button>
            <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onNo}>{t('delete.no')}</Button>
          </ButtonGroup>
        }
      >
        <div className={styles.content}>
          <RuleSummary title={rule.title} description={rule.summary} />
        </div>
      </Sheet>
    )
  }
  return (
    <Sheet
      labelledBy={id}
      onClose={onNo}
      header={<BottomSheetHeader headingId={id} heading={heading} />}
      footer={
        <ButtonGroup aria-label={heading} direction="horizontal">
          <Button variant="secondary" onClick={onNo}>{t('delete.no')}</Button>
          <Button onClick={onYes}>{t('delete.yes')}</Button>
        </ButtonGroup>
      }
    >
      <div className={styles.content}>
        <RuleSummary title={rule.title} description={rule.summary} />
      </div>
    </Sheet>
  )
}

/** Deleted (Figma "Rule deleted" 5612:42455). */
export function RuleDeletedSheet({ onOkay }: { onOkay?: () => void }) {
  const id = useId()
  return (
    <Sheet
      labelledBy={id}
      onClose={onOkay}
      footer={
        <ButtonGroup aria-label={t('deleted.title')}>
          <Button onClick={onOkay}>{t('deleted.okay')}</Button>
        </ButtonGroup>
      }
    >
      <Stack gap="08" align="center" className={[styles.content, styles.centre, styles.roomy].join(' ')}>
        <h2 id={id} className={styles.title}>{t('deleted.title')}</h2>
        <p className={styles.description}>{t('deleted.description')}</p>
      </Stack>
    </Sheet>
  )
}


/**
 * Card style New · a creation's details: one clear next step in the dock, everything else quiet.
 * - header (L3 large): DASH's mark, the name, what it does;
 * - facts: its status (On / Paused · On chart / Not on a chart) and the activity line the card shows;
 * - a Smart Rule says what that means;
 * - a short list of the other actions — Edit with DASH › (indicators), Delete (red, last, apart from the main action);
 * - the dock: Add to chart (an indicator) or Edit with DASH (a rule). Close: tap outside or drag down.
 */
export function CreationDetailsSheet({ item, kind, on: initialOn, onToggle, onClose, onEdit, onDelete }: {
  item: { title: string; summary: string; smart?: boolean; activity: { text: string; strong?: string; after?: string }; activityOff?: { text: string; strong?: string; after?: string } }
  kind: 'rule' | 'indicator'
  /** As it is now (the card's switch). */
  on: boolean
  /** The sheet's own switch (Rule on / Show on chart): turn it on or off right here. */
  onToggle?: (on: boolean) => void
  onClose?: () => void
  /** Edit with DASH: opens it in its chat, ready to change (rules and indicators alike). */
  onEdit?: () => void
  onDelete?: () => void
}) {
  const id = useId()
  // The switch here and the status follow each other (and the page behind, through onToggle).
  const [on, setOn] = useState(initialOn)
  const toggle = (next: boolean) => {
    setOn(next)
    onToggle?.(next)
  }
  // Activity follows the switch: an indicator taken off says so (activityOff), instead of still reading "On your … chart".
  const { text, strong, after } = !on && item.activityOff ? item.activityOff : item.activity
  const status = kind === 'rule' ? (on ? t('details.on') : t('cards.paused')) : on ? t('cards.onChart') : t('details.notOnChart')
  // The dock: Edit (primary, left) and Delete (secondary, right) side by side, for rules and indicators alike. (Adding to a
  // chart is the card's own switch.)
  return (
    <Sheet
      labelledBy={id}
      onClose={onClose}
      header={<BottomSheetHeader size="lg" headingId={id} heading={item.title} description={item.summary} icon={<DashOrb size="md" />}
        tag={item.smart ? <Tag color="success" variant="secondary" size="sm">{t('rules.smart')}</Tag> : undefined} />}
      footer={
        <ButtonGroup aria-label={item.title} direction="horizontal">
          <Button iconLeft={<Icon icon={msEdit} />} onClick={onEdit}>{t('details.edit')}</Button>
          <Button variant="secondary" iconLeft={<Icon icon={msDelete} />} onClick={onDelete}>{t('rules.delete')}</Button>
        </ButtonGroup>
      }
    >
      <Stack gap="16">
        {/* Status: one toggle card — Status (heading) with its activity under it, the on / off word and the switch on
            the right. (Details V1 / V2: archive/dash-history-versions.) */}
        <ListCell
          variant="card"
          as="label"
          label={<span className={styles.statusHeading}>{t('details.status')}</span>}
          description={<span className={styles.activityValue}>{text}{strong && <strong>{strong}</strong>}{after}</span>}
          multiline
          trailing={
            <span className={styles.statusToggle}>
              <span>{status}</span>
              <Switch checked={on} onChange={(e) => toggle(e.target.checked)} aria-label={t('details.switchStatus', { status })} />
            </span>
          }
        />
        {/* Indicators: get the Pine Script behind it — Copy / Download. */}
        {kind === 'indicator' && <PineActions name={item.title} />}
      </Stack>
    </Sheet>
  )
}
```

## Source — shared app parts it uses

### `src/shared/copy.ts`

```ts
/**
 * UI copy. Every user-facing string of a flow lives in ONE file, `src/flows/<flow-id>/copy.json` — flat keys
 * ("empty.title") → the text. Screens read it through the flow's `t`:
 *
 *   t('empty.title')                       → "No search results found"
 *   t('group.results', { list, count })    → "Stocks (8)"   ({name} placeholders are filled in)
 *
 * Sample data (stock names, prices, watchlists) stays in the flow's data.ts — copy.json is only the words the app
 * itself says: titles, labels, buttons, empty states, accessible names. Porting a flow: this file is the string
 * table (Flutter ARB / iOS Localizable.strings).
 */
export type CopyVars = Record<string, string | number>

export function makeCopy<Copy extends Record<string, string>>(flow: string, copy: Copy) {
  return function t(key: keyof Copy & string, vars?: CopyVars): string {
    const template = copy[key] ?? key
    return vars ? template.replace(/\{(\w+)\}/g, (m, name: string) => (name in vars ? String(vars[name]) : m)) : template
  }
}
```

### `src/shared/data/format.ts`

```ts
/** ₹ with Indian grouping: inr(123456.5) → "₹1,23,456.50"; inr(1000, 0) → "₹1,000". */
export const inr = (n: number, decimals = 2) =>
  '₹' + n.toLocaleString('en-IN', { minimumFractionDigits: decimals, maximumFractionDigits: decimals })

/** "9876543210" → "98765 43210" (how Indian mobile numbers are read out). */
export const phone = (digits: string) => (digits.length > 5 ? `${digits.slice(0, 5)} ${digits.slice(5)}` : digits)

/** Keep the last `visible` characters: mask('ABCPM1234K', 1, 5) → "ABCPM****K". */
export const mask = (s: string, keepStart: number, keepEnd: number) =>
  s.slice(0, keepStart) + '•'.repeat(Math.max(0, s.length - keepStart - keepEnd)) + s.slice(s.length - keepEnd)
```

### `src/shared/prototype.ts`

```ts
// Prototype behaviour the flows use — the ONLY way a flow touches the preview (src/preview). In a real app: interactive
// is always true, `go` is the app's navigation, and useAutoAdvance is "when the server answers, go on" (a loader /
// polling step).
import { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useSyncExternalStore } from 'react'

export type Preview = {
  /**
   * Prototype (true): real modal L3 BottomSheets, taps move to the next screen, loaders advance on their own.
   * Board (false): every screen frozen as in the Figma board — sheets are drawn as static surfaces.
   */
  interactive: boolean
  /** Go to another screen of the flow (by id). Does nothing on the board. */
  go: (id: string) => void
  /** The screen being shown — a new id gives the sheet a fresh mount while the page behind it stays put. */
  screenId?: string
}

export const PreviewContext = createContext<Preview>({ interactive: false, go: () => {} })
export const usePreview = () => useContext(PreviewContext)

/** Prototype only: after `ms`, go to `next` (loaders, "Verifying…"). */
export function useAutoAdvance(next: string | undefined, ms: number) {
  const { interactive, go } = usePreview()
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!interactive || !next) return
    const t = window.setTimeout(() => go(next), ms)
    return () => window.clearTimeout(t)
  }, [interactive, next, ms, go])
}

/** How long a loader or "Verifying…" state stays up in the prototype. */
export const LOADING_MS = 1600

// ---- Flow options (prototype settings such as a design version) ----------------------------------------------------
// Picked in the preview (desktop panel, or the settings sheet on a phone), remembered per browser. A real app has no
// such switch: it ships one version.

// The key carries the option's default: when a flow changes its default (e.g. to a new version), earlier picks reset.
const optionKey = (flow: string, option: string, fallback: string) => `prototype-option:${flow}.${option}@${fallback}`
const optionListeners = new Set<() => void>()

function readOption(key: string): string | null {
  try { return localStorage.getItem(key) } catch { return null }
}

/** The preview sets an option (and every screen reading it re-renders). */
export function setFlowOption(flow: string, option: string, fallback: string, value: string) {
  const key = optionKey(flow, option, fallback)
  try { localStorage.setItem(key, value) } catch { /* storage off: this visit only */ }
  memory.set(key, value)
  optionListeners.forEach((l) => l())
}

const memory = new Map<string, string>()

/** A flow's prototype option: the picked value, or `fallback` (the option's default) when none is picked. */
export function useFlowOption(flow: string, option: string, fallback: string) {
  return useSyncExternalStore(
    (onChange) => { optionListeners.add(onChange); return () => { optionListeners.delete(onChange) } },
    () => memory.get(optionKey(flow, option, fallback)) ?? readOption(optionKey(flow, option, fallback)) ?? fallback,
  )
}

type OptionLike = { id: string; default: string; showIf?: Record<string, string[]> }

/** Every option of a flow as it's set now (the settings panel's show / hide and nesting). */
export function useFlowOptionValues(flow: { id: string; options?: OptionLike[] }): Record<string, string> {
  const snap = useSyncExternalStore(
    (onChange) => { optionListeners.add(onChange); return () => { optionListeners.delete(onChange) } },
    () => JSON.stringify(Object.fromEntries((flow.options ?? []).map((o) => {
      const key = optionKey(flow.id, o.id, o.default)
      return [o.id, memory.get(key) ?? readOption(key) ?? o.default]
    }))),
  )
  return JSON.parse(snap)
}

/** Whether an option matters right now (every option it depends on has one of the listed values, all the way up). */
export function optionShown(options: OptionLike[], option: OptionLike, values: Record<string, string>): boolean {
  return Object.entries(option.showIf ?? {}).every(([id, allowed]) => {
    const parent = options.find((o) => o.id === id)
    return allowed.includes(values[id]) && (!parent || optionShown(options, parent, values))
  })
}

/** How deep an option sits under the ones it depends on (0 = top level) — the panel indents it that much. */
export function optionDepth(options: OptionLike[], option: OptionLike): number {
  const parents = Object.keys(option.showIf ?? {}).map((id) => options.find((o) => o.id === id)).filter(Boolean) as OptionLike[]
  return parents.length ? 1 + Math.max(...parents.map((p) => optionDepth(options, p))) : 0
}

/** How many of a flow's options are off their default (the settings panel's badge). */
export function useFlowOptionsChanged(flow: { id: string; options?: { id: string; default: string }[] }) {
  return useSyncExternalStore(
    (onChange) => { optionListeners.add(onChange); return () => { optionListeners.delete(onChange) } },
    () => (flow.options ?? []).filter((o) => {
      const key = optionKey(flow.id, o.id, o.default)
      return (memory.get(key) ?? readOption(key) ?? o.default) !== o.default
    }).length,
  )
}

/**
 * Typing on a phone uses the phone's own keyboard (a touch screen, `pointer: coarse`) — the prototype's drawn keyboard
 * stays hidden. On a laptop the drawn keyboard shows (for the look) and the laptop's keys type into the focused field.
 */
export function useSystemKeyboard() {
  return typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)').matches
}
```

### `src/shared/ui/Screen.module.css`

```css
/*
 * One phone screen: the OS status bar, then the page — top bar, a body that scrolls and fills the space, the bottom
 * bar / button dock — with an optional toast just above the bottom and a sheet over everything.
 */
.screen {
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
  overflow: clip; /* clip, not hidden: a sheet taking focus while it slides in can't scroll the screen */
  background: var(--l3-surface-default);
  color: var(--l3-content-primary);
}

.page {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  flex: 1;
  min-height: 0;
}

.middle {
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  flex: 1;
  min-height: 0;
}

/* Like a phone: no scrollbar that stays on screen — the page, rails and open sheets still scroll (touch, wheel, keys). */
.screen,
.screen * {
  scrollbar-width: none;
}

.screen ::-webkit-scrollbar {
  display: none;
}

.body {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  flex: 1;
  min-height: 0;
  overflow-x: hidden; /* a screen never scrolls sideways — only rails inside it do */
  overflow-y: auto;
}

/* Floating toast: sits on the bottom edge of the body, above the dock / navbar (L3 Aerobar rule). */
.toast {
  position: absolute;
  inset: auto 0 0;
}

/* The prototype's modal L3 sheet is portalled into this screen — lift it above the bottom bars. */
.screen.screen > [data-contained] {
  z-index: var(--app-layer-sheet);
}
```

### `src/shared/ui/Screen.tsx`

```tsx
import { Fragment, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { usePreview } from '../prototype'
import { SheetHost } from './Sheet'
import styles from './Screen.module.css'

type ScreenProps = {
  /** Actionbar (or nothing on full-bleed screens like the welcome screen). */
  top?: ReactNode
  /** Bottom navbar, button dock (ButtonGroup) or the keypad. */
  bottom?: ReactNode
  /** A floating Aerobar toast — shown just above `bottom`. */
  toast?: ReactNode
  /** A Sheet over the screen. */
  sheet?: ReactNode
  /** Screen content: scrolls when taller than the space between `top` and `bottom`. */
  children?: ReactNode
  /** A flow's own styling hook on the screen root (e.g. an experiment scoped to one flow). */
  className?: string
}

/**
 * The frame of every screen: top · body · bottom, a toast above the bottom, and a sheet over it all. It fills the
 * space between the OS status bar and the OS navigation bar (the preview draws those — real apps get them from the
 * OS, edge-to-edge insets), so nothing sits under the gesture handle. The screen is the sheet's container, so sheets
 * and their scrim stay in the app; its SheetHost keeps one sheet open while the screen's sheet changes (no scrim flash
 * between two sheets). Mark a bottom part with data-surface="primary" | "secondary" if the navigation bar should take
 * its colour (the button dock and the bottom navbar are recognised already).
 */
export function Screen({ top, bottom, toast, sheet, children, className }: ScreenProps) {
  const [el, setEl] = useState<HTMLDivElement | null>(null)
  const { screenId } = usePreview()
  return (
    <div ref={setEl} className={[styles.screen, className].filter(Boolean).join(' ')}>
      <SheetHost container={el}>
        <div className={styles.page} data-part="page">
          {top}
          <div className={styles.middle}>
            <div className={styles.body}>{children}</div>
            {toast && <div className={styles.toast}>{toast}</div>}
          </div>
          {bottom}
        </div>
        <Fragment key={screenId}>{sheet}</Fragment>
      </SheetHost>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### `src/shared/ui/Sheet.tsx`

```tsx
import { createContext, useCallback, useContext, useId, useLayoutEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from 'react'
import { BottomSheet, BottomSheetSurface } from '@l3/components/BottomSheet'
import { Overlay } from '@l3/components/Overlay'
import { usePreview } from '../prototype'
import styles from './Sheet.module.css'

/** Lets the L3 sheet play its exit before the next screen replaces it (≈ motion/duration-medium). */
const SHEET_EXIT_MS = 240

type SheetProps = {
  header?: ReactNode
  children?: ReactNode
  /** The button dock — a <ButtonGroup>. */
  footer?: ReactNode
  /** Id of the header's heading (BottomSheetHeader `headingId`). */
  labelledBy?: string
  /** Accessible name when there's no header (loaders). */
  label?: string
  /** Prototype: where a backdrop tap, drag down or Esc goes. Leave out for sheets that can't be dismissed (loaders). */
  onClose?: () => void
  /** A screen's own styling hook on the sheet surface (e.g. a sheet that brings its own layout and no padding). */
  className?: string
}

type Publish = (id: string, sheet: SheetProps | null) => void
const SheetHostContext = createContext<Publish | null>(null)

/**
 * An L3 bottom sheet over the screen.
 * Prototype: the real modal <BottomSheet> (focus trap, drag to close, scrim tap), drawn by the screen's SheetHost —
 * so when one sheet leads to another over the same page, the scrim stays and only the sheet's content changes.
 * Board: the same surface drawn statically with the L3 Overlay — dozens of open modals on one page would fight
 * over focus, so the board shows <BottomSheetSurface>, which is what the modal renders inside.
 */
export function Sheet(props: SheetProps) {
  const { interactive } = usePreview()
  const publish = useContext(SheetHostContext)
  const id = useId()
  const hosted = interactive && publish !== null

  // Hand the latest content to the host on every render; take it back when this sheet goes away.
  useLayoutEffect(() => { if (hosted) publish(id, props) })
  useLayoutEffect(() => (hosted ? () => publish(id, null) : undefined), [hosted, publish, id])

  if (hosted) return null
  const { header, children, footer, labelledBy, label, className } = props
  return (
    <>
      <Overlay open className={styles.scrim} />
      <div className={styles.dock} role="dialog" aria-labelledby={labelledBy} aria-label={label}>
        <BottomSheetSurface header={header} footer={footer} className={className}>{children}</BottomSheetSurface>
      </div>
    </>
  )
}

/**
 * Prototype: one modal L3 BottomSheet per screen, kept open while the screen's sheet changes (sheet → sheet swaps
 * the content in place, no scrim flash or slide). It closes with its exit animation when the screen has no sheet.
 */
export function SheetHost({ container, children }: { container: HTMLElement | null; children: ReactNode }) {
  const [shown, setShown] = useState<{ id: string; sheet: SheetProps; open: boolean } | null>(null)
  const publish = useCallback<Publish>((id, sheet) => {
    setShown((s) => (sheet ? { id, sheet, open: true } : s && s.id === id ? { ...s, open: false } : s))
  }, [])

  const close = () => {
    const onClose = shown?.sheet.onClose
    if (!onClose) return
    setShown((s) => s && { ...s, open: false })
    window.setTimeout(onClose, SHEET_EXIT_MS)
  }

  return (
    <SheetHostContext.Provider value={publish}>
      {children}
      {container && shown && (
        <BottomSheet
          open={shown.open}
          onClose={close}
          container={container}
          header={shown.sheet.header}
          footer={shown.sheet.footer}
          aria-labelledby={shown.sheet.labelledBy}
          aria-label={shown.sheet.label}
          className={shown.sheet.className}
        >
          {shown.sheet.children}
        </BottomSheet>
      )}
    </SheetHostContext.Provider>
  )
}
```

```css
/* OS text keyboard mock (Figma "L3: System keyboard", 260 tall at 360): 5 rows of 40 tall keys on a grey tray. */
.keyboard {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: var(--l3-spacing-08);
  padding: var(--l3-spacing-12) var(--l3-spacing-06) var(--l3-spacing-16);
  /* On a real phone, clear the home indicator (like the L3 button dock does). */
  padding-bottom: calc(var(--l3-spacing-16) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, var(--l3-spacing-00)));
  background: var(--l3-surface-secondary);
}

.row {
  display: flex;
  gap: var(--l3-spacing-04);
}

/* The A–L row is inset by about half a key, like a phone keyboard. */
.row[data-row='2'] {
  padding-inline: var(--l3-spacing-16);
}

.key {
  display: flex;
  flex: 1 1 0;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  min-width: 0;
  height: var(--l3-size-40);
  padding: 0;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: var(--l3-radius-08);
  background: var(--l3-surface-primary);
  color: var(--l3-content-primary);
  font: var(--l3-text-description-18);
  cursor: pointer;
  touch-action: manipulation;
  -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent;
}

.key[data-wide] {
  flex-grow: 1.5;
}

.key[data-kind='space'] {
  flex-grow: 5;
  font: var(--l3-text-label-12);
}

.key[data-kind='fn'] {
  background: var(--l3-surface-tertiary);
  font: var(--l3-text-label-14);
}

/* The keyboard's action key (Search) — the phone's own accent, not an app colour. */
.key[data-kind='go'] {
  background: var(--l3-surface-accent-discover-default);
  color: var(--l3-content-inverted);
}

.key :is(svg, span):not(.popup) {
  width: var(--l3-icon-size-20);
  height: var(--l3-icon-size-20);
}

/* Function keys (Shift, Delete, ?123, Space, Enter): pressed, they darken and give a little. */
.key:not([data-kind='letter'])[data-held] {
  background-image: linear-gradient(var(--l3-state-layer-dark-pressed), var(--l3-state-layer-dark-pressed));
  transform: scale(var(--l3-motion-scale-press-default));
}

/*
 * Letter keys: while held, a magnified bubble of the key pops up above it (Gboard / iPhone): the key's width plus a
 * little, two keys tall, the character large near its top; it grows out of the key (120 ms). The key itself dims under
 * it. Keys at a row's ends keep the bubble inside the keyboard's edge.
 */
.key {
  position: relative;
}

.key[data-kind='letter'][data-held] {
  background: var(--l3-surface-tertiary);
}

.popup {
  position: absolute;
  bottom: 0;
  left: 50%;
  z-index: 2;
  display: flex;
  justify-content: center;
  box-sizing: border-box;
  width: calc(100% + var(--l3-spacing-12));
  height: calc(var(--l3-size-40) * 2 + var(--l3-spacing-08));
  padding-top: var(--l3-spacing-06);
  border-radius: var(--l3-radius-12);
  background: var(--l3-surface-primary);
  box-shadow: var(--l3-shadow-elevation-high);
  color: var(--l3-content-primary);
  font: var(--l3-text-heading-28);
  pointer-events: none;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
  transform-origin: 50% 100%;
  animation: key-pop var(--l3-motion-duration-short) var(--l3-motion-easing-decelerate) both;
}

.key[data-edge='start'] .popup {
  left: 0;
  transform: none;
  transform-origin: 0 100%;
}

.key[data-edge='end'] .popup {
  right: 0;
  left: auto;
  transform: none;
  transform-origin: 100% 100%;
}

@keyframes key-pop {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    scale: 0.6;
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .key:not([data-kind='letter'])[data-held] {
    transform: none;
  }

  .popup {
    animation: none;
  }
}
```

### `src/shared/ui/TextKeyboard.tsx`

```tsx
import { useState, type PointerEvent } from 'react'
import { Icon } from '@l3/components/Icon'
import { msArrowUpward, msBackspace, msKeyboardTab } from '@l3/icons/material'
import styles from './TextKeyboard.module.css'

type Key = { key: string; label?: string; kind?: 'letter' | 'fn' | 'space' | 'go'; wide?: boolean }

const ROWS: Key[][] = [
  '1234567890'.split('').map((k) => ({ key: k })),
  'QWERTYUIOP'.split('').map((k) => ({ key: k })),
  'ASDFGHJKL'.split('').map((k) => ({ key: k })),
  [{ key: 'Shift', kind: 'fn', wide: true }, ...'ZXCVBNM'.split('').map((k) => ({ key: k })), { key: 'Backspace', kind: 'fn', wide: true }],
  [{ key: '?123', kind: 'fn', wide: true }, { key: ',' }, { key: ' ', label: 'EN • LV', kind: 'space' }, { key: '.' }, { key: 'Enter', kind: 'go', wide: true }],
]

/**
 * The phone's own text keyboard (OS chrome, NOT part of the app or L3 — Figma "L3: System keyboard", isNumeric =
 * False). Drawn so search screens read like the phone; in the prototype the keys type into the screen. Real apps get the
 * system keyboard by focusing the text field (search: `enterKeyHint="search"`). `data-surface` tells the OS navigation
 * bar below it to take the keyboard's grey.
 */
export function TextKeyboard({ onKey }: { onKey?: (key: string) => void }) {
  // The key being held: a letter / digit / punctuation key shows its pop-up (a magnified bubble above it, like Gboard and
  // the iPhone keyboard) until the finger lifts; function keys just darken.
  const [held, setHeld] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const release = () => setHeld(null)
  return (
    <div className={styles.keyboard} role="group" aria-label="Keyboard" data-surface="secondary">
      {ROWS.map((row, i) => (
        <div key={i} className={styles.row} data-row={i}>
          {row.map((k, j) => (
            <button
              key={k.key}
              type="button"
              className={styles.key}
              data-kind={k.kind ?? 'letter'}
              data-wide={k.wide || undefined}
              data-held={held === k.key || undefined}
              data-edge={j === 0 ? 'start' : j === row.length - 1 ? 'end' : undefined}
              aria-label={label(k)}
              onPointerDown={(e) => {
                keepFocus(e)
                setHeld(k.key)
              }}
              onPointerUp={release}
              onPointerLeave={release}
              onPointerCancel={release}
              onClick={() => onKey?.(k.key)}
            >
              {k.key === 'Shift' ? <Icon icon={msArrowUpward} /> : k.key === 'Backspace' ? <Icon icon={msBackspace} /> : k.key === 'Enter' ? <Icon icon={msKeyboardTab} /> : (k.label ?? k.key)}
              {(k.kind ?? 'letter') === 'letter' && held === k.key && (
                <span className={styles.popup} aria-hidden="true">{k.label ?? k.key}</span>
              )}
            </button>
          ))}
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  )
}

const label = (k: Key) =>
  ({ Shift: 'Shift', Backspace: 'Delete', Enter: 'Search', ' ': 'Space', '?123': 'Numbers and symbols' } as Record<string, string>)[k.key]

/** Like the OS keyboard, a key press doesn't take focus: the field being typed into keeps its Typing state. */
const keepFocus = (e: PointerEvent) => e.preventDefault()

/** Apply a keyboard key to a text value: letters, digits, space, comma, full stop and delete (Shift / ?123 do nothing here). */
export const typeText = (value: string, key: string) => {
  if (key === 'Backspace') return value.slice(0, -1)
  if (key.length !== 1) return value
  // Like a phone keyboard: the first letter is a capital, the rest lower case.
  return value + (value === '' ? key.toUpperCase() : key.toLowerCase())
}
```

### `src/shared/ui/dash/DashOrb.module.css`

```css
/*
 * The orb artwork is the Figma vector component: every part keeps the exact Figma box (px inside a 100 × 100 frame —
 * artwork geometry, not layout), and the whole thing scales to the slot. Sizes come from L3 size tokens.
 */
.orb {
  --orb-box: var(--l3-size-96);
  position: relative;
  display: inline-block;
  flex: none;
  width: var(--orb-box);
  height: var(--orb-box);
}

.orb[data-size='lg'] { --orb-box: var(--l3-size-96); }
.orb[data-size='md'] { --orb-box: var(--l3-size-64); }
.orb[data-size='sm'] { --orb-box: var(--l3-size-32); }

/* The art is drawn at 100 and scaled to the box. */
.scale {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0;
  left: 0;
  width: 100px;
  height: 100px;
  transform: scale(calc(var(--orb-box) / 100px));
  transform-origin: 0 0;
}

.art {
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
}

/* Figma: the halo copy sits 8 right / 10 down, layer blur 23.35. */
.halo {
  transform: translate(8px, 10px);
  filter: blur(var(--app-dash-orb-halo-blur));
}

.art img {
  display: block;
  max-width: none;
}

/* "Group 1000006113" (back leaf, blurred glow): box 55.5 × 57.8, bottom 49.7, centre +17.2. */
.leafBackBox,
.leafFrontBox {
  position: absolute;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  transform: translateX(-50%);
}

.leafBackBox {
  bottom: 49.71px;
  left: calc(50% + 17.24px);
  width: 55.526px;
  height: 57.791px;
}

.leafBack,
.leafFront {
  position: relative;
  flex: none;
  /* Figma's order: rotate, then skew, then the vertical flip (Tailwind -scale-y-100 rotate-[-108.93deg] skew-x-1) */
  transform: rotate(-108.93deg) skewX(1deg) scaleY(-1);
}

.leafBack {
  width: 45.469px;
  height: 43.372px;
}

.leafBackImg {
  position: absolute;
  inset: -14.91% -14.25% -14.71% -13.92%;
  width: auto;
  height: auto;
}

/* "Group 1000006112" (front leaves). */
.leafFrontBox {
  bottom: 50.97px;
  left: calc(50% + 17.61px);
  width: 50.159px;
  height: 51.373px;
}

.leafFront {
  width: 40.069px;
  height: 39.526px;
}

.leafFront img {
  width: 100%;
  height: 100%;
}

/* "Ellipse 8": the ring's soft inner fill. */
.fill {
  position: absolute;
  top: 30.85px;
  left: 10.38px;
  width: 57.662px;
  height: 59.282px;
}

/* "circleGroup": the angular-gradient ring. */
.ringBox {
  position: absolute;
  top: 27.88px;
  left: 7.5px;
  width: 62.852px;
  height: 64.618px;
}

.ring {
  position: absolute;
  inset: -7.11% -7.31%;
  width: auto;
  height: auto;
}

/*
 * Idle motion (live app, 2026-10-23): the ring's yellow highlight goes round clockwise once a second, at a steady
 * speed — the ring and its soft fill turn on their own centres; the leaves stay still. Off for reduced motion.
 */
.ringBox,
.fill {
  animation: dash-orb-spin var(--app-dash-orb-spin) linear infinite;
}

@keyframes dash-orb-spin {
  to {
    transform: rotate(1turn);
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .ringBox,
  .fill {
    animation: none;
  }
}
```

### `src/shared/ui/dash/DashOrb.tsx`

```tsx
import leafBack from './assets/leaf-back.svg'
import leafFront from './assets/leaf-front.svg'
import orbFill from './assets/orb-fill.svg'
import orbRing from './assets/orb-ring.svg'
import styles from './DashOrb.module.css'

export type DashOrbSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'

/**
 * DASH's mascot — the lime ring with two leaves (Figma "Logo" / "BotIcon", the 100 × 100 vector component), drawn from
 * its own vector parts in the Figma positions, with the soft halo behind it (a blurred copy).
 * Sizes: lg 96 (landing pages), md 64 (sheet headers, on a soft disc), sm 32 (the rule card's icon). The DASH pill sets its own
 * box (21.8). Shared: DASH flows and the home's entry pill use the same artwork.
 * Decorative: screen readers skip it — the text next to it says what it is.
 */
export function DashOrb({ size = 'lg', halo = true }: { size?: DashOrbSize; halo?: boolean }) {
  return (
    <span className={styles.orb} data-size={size} aria-hidden="true">
      <span className={styles.scale}>
        {halo && <OrbArt className={styles.halo} />}
        <OrbArt />
      </span>
    </span>
  )
}

/** The artwork at its Figma size (100 × 100); the parent scales it. */
function OrbArt({ className }: { className?: string }) {
  return (
    <span className={[styles.art, className].filter(Boolean).join(' ')}>
      <span className={styles.leafBackBox}>
        <span className={styles.leafBack}>
          <img src={leafBack} alt="" className={styles.leafBackImg} />
        </span>
      </span>
      <span className={styles.leafFrontBox}>
        <span className={styles.leafFront}>
          <img src={leafFront} alt="" />
        </span>
      </span>
      <img src={orbFill} alt="" className={styles.fill} />
      <span className={styles.ringBox}>
        <img src={orbRing} alt="" className={styles.ring} />
      </span>
    </span>
  )
}
```
